title: Is The Cheapest Specialized Tarmac SL8 Actually Good?

takeaways.text: The FACT 10r frame is less stiff than the S-Works but still reactive, and the reviewer prefers it for comfort; it does not ride like its weight.
Bars are too wide across the size range (40 cm on a 52, 42 cm on a 54) and cranks long (172.5 mm on a 54), which he calls old-school fitting for an aero bike.
Positives: most of the S-Works aero shapes and geometry, brass spoke nipples and an excellent 105 Di2 groupset with wide gearing.
The size-52 bike weighed 7.9 kg, more than the advertised figure for a 56; narrow rims and 26 mm tires hold back comfort and should be upgraded first.

disclosure: Publication review; the video carries a Magene power-meter sponsorship. The entry Tarmac SL8 reviewed uses the same FACT 10r frame and 105 Di2 as the candidate; trim naming varies by market.
summary: road.cc's review of the cheapest Specialized Tarmac SL8 with 105 Di2, compared with the S-Works version.
